summary: Approved Goldilocks ‘too much’ scene: Patch stands stalled at an outdoor trail junction while physically overloaded by expedition tools, maps, notes, guides, bags, and conflicting route signs. The scene visualizes excessive context and tooling becoming a burden that prevents a confident next move.

composition: Landscape outdoor adventure scene with Patch centered in the foreground at a branching forest trail.
Patch is shown full body and fills much of the central frame, with signposts on both sides and mountains/trees behind.
The camera is a close-to-medium frontal three-quarter view that makes the accumulated gear visually dominant.
Loose maps, plans, a checklist, and a guidebook occupy the ground around Patch, extending the overload beyond what he can carry.
patch_design: Canonical teal hood frames an off-white face panel with simple black oval eyes and small white highlights.
Two dark hood antennae with rounded tips are visible.
Patch wears dark trousers, teal shoes with white soles, and a dark crossbody bag with a white greater-than mark.
Patch has exactly one left arm and one right arm; the visible hands are occupied naturally without duplicated limbs.
Facial expression is worried and uncertain rather than angry or villainous.
props_and_environment: A pickaxe and shovel are strapped behind Patch as practical expedition tools.
A heavy coil of rope hangs around Patch’s shoulder and upper body.
Additional kit includes rolled maps, lantern, compass, pouches, notebooks, guidebooks, clipped notes, and planning sheets.
Conflicting wooden route signs include directions such as THIS WAY, THAT WAY, SCENIC ROUTE, SHORTCUT, SAFE PATH, ADVANCED TRAIL, EXPERT ONLY, and NOPE.
The setting is a bright wooded mountain trail with warm daylight and clear adventure framing.
scene_semantics: The core metaphor is overload: more information and more tools do not automatically create a better next move.
The physical weight of tools and guidance is as important as the volume of documents.
Patch is ready for an adventure in principle but is immobilized by competing instructions and excessive preparation.

positive_constraints: Preserve canonical Patch identity and the single visible crossbody bag with white greater-than mark.
Keep the outdoor trail/junction framing and bright Adventures editorial style.
Make the overload physical as well as informational: real expedition tools, rope, maps, guides, notes, and route signs should visibly burden Patch.
Keep Patch worried/confused but friendly and non-aggressive.
Use the image as the ‘too much’ pole of a three-image Goldilocks guidance-balance set.
negative_constraints: Do not simplify the scene into paperwork-only clutter; practical tools are part of the metaphor.
Do not turn Patch into a generic robot, human, toy, or glossy mascot.
Do not add extra arms, duplicated hands, duplicated Patch figures, or impossible limb attachments.
Do not make the overload feel like random hoarding; props should read as plausible journey preparation, guidance, and route-selection material.
Do not treat any individual sign or guide as the uniquely correct route; the problem is competing abundance.
